deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on tame topology ('topologie modérée') from 1974. The preceding page sketches manifolds with boundary fibred over manifolds with boundary, and the following page is headed 'Équisingularité'. This page sets up the combinatorial skeleton of the 'dévissage' of a nice stratified space into manifolds with boundary or corners and fibrations between them.

Set-up: X is a stratified space with open strata V_i^° of dimension n_i, partially ordered by incidence (V_j ⊂ closure of V_i). Remove a tubular neighbourhood of all lower strata from V_i, or equivalently take its real oriented blow-up or 'unzipping'. The result is a compact manifold with corners V_i whose boundary has faces ∂_j V_i^°, one for each lower stratum j. Each face fibres over (the compactified) V_j^°: ∂_j V_i^° → V_j^°. The fibre is the part, inside stratum i, of the link of V_j.

First formula: the boundary of the face ∂_j V_i^° (dimension n_i−1) splits into two kinds of piece.
(1) Corners ∂_j V_i^° | ∂_k V_j^°, for k below j. This is the part of the face lying over the boundary face ∂_k V_j of V_j, and it maps to V_k^°.
(2) A 'vertical' part ∂^{(1)} ∂_j V_i^°. This is the fibrewise boundary of the link bundle, and it still maps to V_j^°.
So the corner structure of V_i is compatible with that of V_j under the fibration. These are the familiar axioms of an iterated fibration structure, or of Thom–Mather control data.

Middle diagram: an attempt to write down the whole tower for a chain i > j > k > l, with dimensions noted. Rows are V_i ⊃ ∂V_i ⊃ V_ij ⊃ ∂V_ij ⊃ V_ij|∂V_j → V_ijk ← V_ijk|∂V_k ← V_ijkl, and then the same tower for j and for k. Vertical maps are the boundary fibrations, and the squares are marked × (cartesian). Dimension labels n_i, n_i−1, n_i−1, n_i−2, …, n_i−3 track codimension. Some labels on the page are hesitant: under V_ijk there is a mixed 'n_j−2' / 'n_i−2'.

Bottom diagram: the clean version. There is a triangular 'staircase' of spaces V_{ij…p}, one for each chain i > j > … > p of strata. It has:
- horizontal maps V_{ij…q} ← V_{ij…qr} (inclusion of the deeper corner);
- vertical maps V_{ij…} → V_{j…} (forgetting the top index, i.e. the link fibration);
- every square cartesian, so V_{ijk} ≅ V_{ij} ×_{V_j} V_{jk}, and so on;
- the last column V_{ij…p} → V_{j…p} → … → V_p^° being an iterated tower of fibrations over the deepest stratum.
This is a functor from the poset of chains of strata (a nerve or simplicial picture) to manifolds with corners and fibrations. Its 'gluing' should recover X up to tame homeomorphism. This is exactly the equivalence 'stratified space ⇔ system of manifolds with boundary and fibrations' that Grothendieck later advertised in the Esquisse d'un programme (§5) as the dévissage theorem expected in tame topology.
errors: Notation is inconsistent within the middle diagram: V_ij appears both as a boundary face of V_i and as having boundary ∂V_ij. Some dimension labels are uncertain ('n_j−2' vs 'n_i−2' under V_ijk; V_ijkl labelled n_i−3).

Cartesianity (V_ijk = V_ij ×_{V_j} V_jk) only holds if V_ij → V_j is a fibre bundle over the compactified, cornered V_j, i.e. if the control data are compatible. This is an assumption, not proved here.
The orientation of arrows changes between the middle diagram (mixed → and ←) and the final diagram (all horizontal arrows ←). This is draft-level, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Resolution of a stratified space into manifolds with corners whose boundary faces fibre over lower strata (∂_j V_i → V_j), with compatible corner structure ∂(∂_j V_i) = ∪_k ∂_j V_i|∂_k V_j ∪ ∂^{(1)}∂_j V_i
ideas.modern_name: Thom–Mather control data / iterated fibration structure / unzipping (resolution) of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970), Verona (1984), Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza and Albin–Melrose (2010s), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6: dévissage of tame stratified structures into manifolds with boundary and fibrations

ideas.what: Triangular staircase of corner strata V_{ij…p} indexed by chains of strata, with all squares cartesian (V_{ijk} = V_{ij} ×_{V_j} V_{jk})
ideas.modern_name: Functor from the poset of flags/chains of strata to manifolds with corners; diagram description of a conically smooth stratified space / exit-path data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Verona (abstract stratifications); Albin–Melrose; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; implicitly in Goresky–MacPherson style link bundles
ideas.where_published: Spirit announced in Esquisse §5. The explicit cartesian staircase is not in any published text I know of.

ideas.what: Dimension bookkeeping n_i, n_i−1, n_i−2, … along faces and corners
ideas.modern_name: codimension of corners in a manifold with corners

missed.claim: Dated 1974, this shows that Grothendieck already had the explicit cartesian 'staircase' of iterated link fibrations indexed by chains of strata. This is a decade before the Esquisse sketch and close to the modern Albin–Melrose / Ayala–Francis–Tanaka formulations. It is a priority and historical detail rather than a new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the early origin of the dévissage programme in tame topology. It may help historians connect the Esquisse claims to concrete 1974 constructions. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, early sketch of the manifold-with-corners / iterated-fibration resolution of a stratified space with cartesian compatibility squares. The idea is known in the literature (Mather, Verona, Albin–Melrose, AFT) and was announced by Grothendieck himself in the Esquisse. Only the 1974 date and the explicit diagram are mildly notable.
transcription_corrections: Index set under the union: written 'k ∈ 𝒥' (or possibly 'k < j'); unclear in the image.

In the middle diagram the second-row segment reads 'V_{jk}^° → ∂V_{jk}^° ← V_{jk}^°|∂V_k^° ← V_{jkl}^°'. In the first row, '⊃ ∂V_{ij}^° ⊃ V_{ij}^°|∂V_j^°' carries labels 'n_i−2' and 'n_j−2' ('n_j−2c'); the label under V_{ijk} is ambiguous.
Third row of the middle diagram: 'V_k^° ← ∂V_{kl}^° ← V_{kl}^°' with V_{kl}^° ↓ V_l^° below it.
Bottom staircase: the last entries read 'V_{kl…p}' and 'V_{l…p}' (no ° in the image), and there is a dashed continuation before V_p^°.
